summary.intent: Execute Phase 35 (Phala Testnet TEE Migration) end-to-end: restructure TEE worker into monorepo apps/, integrate shared packages, add unit tests, Phala SDK, staging infra, documentation, and deploy a live CVM to Phala Cloud.
summary.outcome: All 6 plans completed across 4 waves with a live CVM running on Phala Cloud production infrastructure, epoch key determinism verified, end-to-end IPNS republish validated, and phase marked complete. Documentation corrected to reflect 'production' instead of 'testnet'.

repo: TEE worker was moved from root `tee-worker/` to `apps/tee-worker/` and now uses shared monorepo packages: `@cipherbox/crypto` for ECIES, `@cipherbox/core` for IPNS signing, `@cipherbox/sdk-core` for KuboProvider/PsaProvider.
Phala Cloud has no separate testnet — the free tier ($20 credit) runs on production nodes (dstack-pha-prod5). 'Testnet' in phase name and docs was a misnomer.
GitHub staging environment now has `PHALA_CLOUD_API_KEY` (secret) and `PHALA_TEE_WORKER_URL` (variable) configured.
TEE worker Docker image published as `ghcr.io/fsm1/cipherbox-tee-worker:v35-amd64`.
Republish latency from remote client to Phala Cloud CVM is ~1155ms avg — network-bound, not compute-bound; co-located deployment will be much faster.
56 unit tests cover TEE-specific orchestration: key derivation, epoch fallback, auth middleware, republish batch processing.
deploy-staging.yml gained `build-tee` and `deploy-tee-phala` jobs; staging docker-compose no longer runs tee-worker locally.

code.finding: Republish route requires ECIES-encrypted IPNS key via `wrapKey`/`unwrapKey` from `@cipherbox/crypto`; test payloads must be properly encrypted with the CVM's derived public key.
Key manager uses `wrapKey`/`unwrapKey` from `@cipherbox/crypto` for ECIES operations; epoch keys are derived deterministically from Phala dstack-sdk and persist across CVM restarts.
Phala CVM docker-compose uses envsubst for `PHALA_TEE_WORKER_URL`, `TEE_WORKER_SECRET`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER`, and `TAG` substitution before `phala deploy`.
Updated to correct 'testnet' to 'production Phala Cloud' throughout; clarifies no separate testnet exists.

workflow: Parallel subagent execution with git worktrees can cause `git config` lock contention — running agents sequentially instead of parallel resolved this.
When agent worktrees produce merge conflicts in STATE.md, taking the agent's version is correct (it reflects the latest completed state).
GSD pause-work/resume-work handoff cycle works well across machine boundaries — credentials, remaining tasks, and context survived the session transfer cleanly.
After `git pull` showed 'Already up to date' twice before showing new commits, a explicit `git fetch --all && git pull` from the Docker host was needed to see updated branch.
The `classifyHandoffIfNeeded` Claude Code runtime bug may fire on agent completion but spot-checks (SUMMARY.md + commits) are the reliable completion signal.
Parallel wave agents should use `--no-verify` on commits; orchestrator runs pre-commit hooks once post-wave.
HANDOFF.json is a one-shot artifact — should be deleted after successful resumption.

friction: Wave 2 parallel execution failed: 35-02 hit a git config lock from parallel worktree spawning, 35-03 was cut off by a usage limit mid-execution — had to re-run both sequentially.
Usage limit hit mid-session required user to type 'continue please' to resume.
CVM restart took several minutes with repeated health check failures before coming back online — no exponential backoff in polling logic.
Docker build/push couldn't run from the main dev machine (Docker daemon at 192.168.133.12) — required a session transfer via pause-work/resume-work to the Docker host.
Memory file had stale Docker host IP (192.168.133.114 vs correct 192.168.133.12) that needed correction mid-session.
Phase name 'phala-testnet-tee-migration' was a misnomer from the start — required post-completion doc corrections across multiple files.
